title: Modbus TCP
summary: Modbus TCP carries the simple Modbus request/response protocol over TCP/IP (port 502). A client (often the PLC) polls registers in a server (a transmitter, drive or meter).

sections.heading: Data model
sections.body: Modbus defines four tables: coils (read/write bits), discrete inputs (read-only bits), holding registers (read/write 16-bit words) and input registers (read-only words). Each request names a **function code**, a start **address** and a **quantity**. Common function codes: 01 read coils, 02 read discrete inputs, **03 read holding registers**, **04 read input registers**, 05/06 write single, 15/16 write multiple.

sections.heading: The MBAP header
sections.body: Modbus TCP prefixes each PDU with the MBAP header: transaction identifier (matches responses to requests), protocol identifier (0), length and **unit identifier**. Gateways use the unit identifier to address serial devices behind them; many TCP devices ignore it.

sections.heading: Addressing pitfalls
sections.body: The protocol uses **zero-based** addresses. Documentation often shows the classic notation 40001 for the first holding register, which is protocol address 0. Mixing the two shifts every value by one register. 32-bit values (REAL, DINT) occupy two registers and the **word order** differs between devices.

sections.heading: Exception responses
sections.body:
| Code | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| 01 | Illegal function (function code not supported) |
| 02 | Illegal data address (register not available) |
| 03 | Illegal data value |
| 04 | Server device failure |
| 0A | Gateway path unavailable |
| 0B | Gateway target device failed to respond |

sections.heading: In PLC Lab
sections.body: PLC Lab simulates Modbus TCP behaviorally: the PLC polls servers with FC03/FC04, honors subnet rules, ARP resolution, connection refusal, timeouts, exception codes 01/02/0B, unit identifier handling and word order. Latency is a fixed educational value. **SIMULATION APPROXIMATION**: this is not a conformance-tested implementation.

modeled: Subnet, gateway, ARP, connection refused and timeout behavior
approximated: Fixed one-way latency; TCP connection setup abstracted to round trips
